question: What defines a safe injection in healthcare delivery?

options.A: It is always administered intramuscularly using glass syringes
options.B: It is cheaper than taking oral medications
options.C: It uses a multi-dose vial for multiple patients
options.D: It causes no harm to the recipient or healthcare worker

explanation: Safety in injections ensures zero harm to both the patient receiving it and the nurse administering it. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T6#GNS122_U4_T6_h1)

question: Why is changing only the needle while reusing the plastic syringe dangerous?

options.A: It causes the medication to expire faster inside the barrel
options.B: It makes the injection more painful for the patient
options.C: It increases the manufacturing cost of the injection
options.D: It still allows blood and pathogens to enter the syringe barrel

explanation: Pathogens can contaminate the syringe body during aspiration, meaning a new needle does not prevent cross-infection. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T6#GNS122_U4_T6_h1)

question: Why do many patients demand injections over oral medications?

options.A: Injections are always provided free of charge
options.B: Swallowing pills is illegal in certain communities
options.C: They believe injections work much faster and are stronger
options.D: Injections do not cause any local skin reactions

explanation: A common cultural belief is that piercing the skin delivers a more potent and rapid healing effect than oral drugs. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T6#GNS122_U4_T6_h2)

question: A patient insists on getting an antibiotic injection for a mild cold. What usually drives this request?

options.A: The belief that injections work faster than pills
options.B: Strict hospital policies on antimicrobial stewardship
options.C: Complete absence of any primary healthcare facilities

explanation: Patients frequently request injections because they assume it cures illnesses quicker than oral treatment. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T6#GNS122_U4_T6_h2)

question: What is a major provider-related cause of unnecessary injections?

options.A: Mandatory peer-review audits in every shift
options.B: Outdated clinical training and misconceptions about drug efficacy
options.C: Excessive availability of oral medications in clinics

explanation: Clinicians who rely on old habits rather than current evidence often prescribe unnecessary injections. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T6#GNS122_U4_T6_h3)

question: How do provider misconceptions about injections affect patient safety?

options.A: They eliminate the need for proper sharps disposal
options.B: They lead to overuse of injections and avoidable complications
options.C: They reduce the overall cost of treating common infections
options.D: They guarantee faster discharge from the ward

explanation: When providers believe injections are always superior, they expose patients to unneeded risks like nerve injury and abscesses. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T6#GNS122_U4_T6_h3)

question: Why do some private clinics heavily promote injections to clients?

options.A: Government policy requires a minimum injection rate per day
options.C: Injections reduce the time spent writing medical records
options.D: Injections often yield higher financial profits for the facility

explanation: Financial gain incentivizes providers to dispense injections because they command higher service and product fees. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T6#GNS122_U4_T6_h4)

question: How does a fee-for-service healthcare model influence injection rates?

options.A: It forces clinics to give away free syringes
options.B: It ensures all patients receive equal medical attention
options.C: It encourages giving more treatments to increase total revenue
options.D: It completely stops the use of intramuscular medications

explanation: When facilities profit directly from each item sold, staff are more likely to prescribe unnecessary drugs. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T6#GNS122_U4_T6_h4)

question: What systemic problem directly forces staff to reuse injection equipment?

options.A: Severe shortages of single-use disposable syringes
options.B: Excessive funding for primary healthcare centers
options.C: An overabundance of safety disposal boxes
options.D: Strict enforcement of infection control laws

explanation: A lack of basic commodities like disposable syringes drives desperate clinicians to reuse unsafe equipment. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T6#GNS122_U4_T6_h5)

question: Which hazard arises when clinics lack proper puncture-proof safety boxes?

options.A: Needlestick injuries and transmission of bloodborne viruses
options.B: Increased resistance of bacteria to oral antibiotics
options.C: Higher out-of-pocket costs for buying intravenous fluids

explanation: Without proper disposal containers, exposed needles easily cause accidental pricks and spread infections like hepatitis and HIV. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T6#GNS122_U4_T6_h5)

question: What is a common localized complication of poorly administered intramuscular injections?
explanation: Poor technique or unsterile equipment leads directly to localized tissue damage, swelling, and nerve injury. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T6#GNS122_U4_T6_h6)

question: Which bloodborne viruses are most commonly transmitted by unsterile injection practices?

options.B: Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, and HIV

explanation: Sharing needles transfers bloodborne pathogens directly into the bloodstream of subsequent patients. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T6#GNS122_U4_T6_h6)

question: What is a primary nursing action to help reduce unnecessary injections?

options.A: Hiding all syringes to prevent doctors from prescribing them
options.B: Replacing all intravenous drips with local herbal remedies
options.C: Discharging patients before they receive medication
options.D: Educating patients on the effectiveness of oral medications

explanation: Nurses use health education to address patient misconceptions and reduce the demand for unnecessary injections. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T6#GNS122_U4_T6_h7)

question: How does placing safety boxes at every point of care protect nursing staff?

options.A: It guarantees that the clinic will never experience shortages
options.B: It automatically sterilizes used needles within five minutes
options.C: It prevents patients from demanding intravenous drugs
options.D: It allows immediate, safe disposal without walking with exposed needles

explanation: Immediate disposal at the bedside prevents accidental needlestick injuries caused by carrying used sharps across rooms. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T6#GNS122_U4_T6_h7)
